oneliner: One WAF rule with a catastrophic-backtracking regex was pushed to the whole fleet at once — CPU hit 100% everywhere and much of the web 502'd for ~27 minutes.
summary: A new managed WAF rule contained a regular expression with catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS). It was deployed globally in one step, with no staged/canary rollout and no CPU bound on rule evaluation. On live traffic the regex went exponential, saturating CPU across Cloudflare's edge and returning 502s worldwide. A recent change had moved WAF execution in a way that removed an earlier CPU protection. Recovery came from a global 'WAF kill switch'. No single broken component: a pathological regex + global simultaneous rollout + a removed safeguard.
source: Cloudflare, 'Details of the Cloudflare outage on July 2, 2019' (John Graham-Cumming)
crosslink: A regex/parser pathology — see ../../parser-differentials (ReDoS is a recognizer blowing up on crafted/ordinary input).
